title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD and Roadmap (v24)
author: Sofia Mendes
body:
Overview

Purpose
This document presents the v24 product overview, PRD, design decisions, roadmap themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for Redwood Inference Unified Inference. It is intended for product, eng, go-to-market, and customer success stakeholders responsible for planning, implementing, and shipping the next major release.

Scope
Covers hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes, focusing on:
- API and SDK surface changes required for new routing and cost controls.
- Requirements for rollout, telemetry and evals.
- Design specs for the routing policy engine and cost-aware fallback.
- Pricing and packaging options aligned with Dedicated commitments.
- Release notes and rollout plan for v24.

Background and Problem Statement
Over the last 18 months customers have asked for tighter cost control primitives, predictable unit economics for mixed workloads, and fewer manual model-fallbacks during capacity events. Existing routing policies are effective but lack per-route SLAs and per-customer cost budgets tied to routing behaviors. v24 aims to address these gaps with a cost-aware unified routing layer, per-route SLAs, and pricing packages that better align revenue to reserved capacity.

Goals and Non-Goals
Goals:
1) Provide per-route SLAs (P50/P95 latency and availability) and enforceable cost budgets at the customer and route level.
2) Introduce a cost-aware fallback engine that chooses compatible model variants to preserve availability within a configured cost envelope.
3) Offer new pricing SKUs for Reserved Capacity with burst allowances and predictable per-token unit pricing.
4) Ensure rollout is safe with canary, A/B, and automatic rollback based on evals and traffic.

Non-Goals:
- Model architecture changes or changes to internal model weights.
- Replacing third-party observability; only we will add tracing hooks and events.

Key Features (high level)
- Per-route SLA definitions and enforcement: routes can declare latency and availability targets.
- Cost-aware fallback engine: routing decision considers cost delta, latency impact, and quality delta.
- Budget enforcement: customer- and route-level budgets that trigger automated policy changes.
- Pricing and packaging: new Reserved Plus SKU that bundles reserved throughput, burst credits, and discounted off-peak units.
- Rollout tooling: integrated rollout policies with automatic traffic shaping and rollback triggers.

Product Requirements (PRD)
Functional Requirements
1) Route SLA API: Routes must support declarative SLA fields: latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, availability_pct.
2) Budget API: Customers can set monthly budget_usd and per-route budget_usd.
3) Fallback engine: Given a primary model, engine returns a ranked list of alternatives with estimated cost_delta_pct and expected latency increase_ms.
4) Telemetry: Emit decision events for each routing decision with fields: route_id, model_attempted, model_selected, cost_estimate_usd, quality_score_estimate.
5) Admin console: Console must surface budgets, SLA violations, and a per-token cost heatmap.

Non-Functional Requirements
- Latency overhead: routing decision must add <= 5ms median overhead for synchronous requests.
- Reliability: routing fallback must be available in 99.95% of requests.
- Security: budget and routing configs must respect RBAC and be visible only to authorized users.
- Observability: metrics must be available in the Console and via exported Prometheus metrics and traces.

Acceptance Criteria
- End-to-end e2e tests demonstrating SLA enforcement for synthetic workloads (P95 <= target for at least 95% of test windows).
- Billing validation for Reserved Plus SKU that matches simulated usage for 5 representative customers.
- Production canary for 5% of traffic with automatic rollback on defined eval regression (>2% quality drop).

Design Spec (technical summary)
Architecture Overview
- New Routing Policy Service (RPS) is a logically separate microservice in the control plane. RPS provides ranked model candidates and budget-aware selection. Runtime nodes call RPS with a small decision context (route_id, customer_id, prompt_len_estimate, latency_budget_ms).

Components
- Routing Policy Service (control plane): Stores policies, budgets, and SLA definitions. Provides gRPC API: EvaluateRoute(ctx, DecisionRequest) -> DecisionResponse.
- Fallback Catalog: Precomputed compatibility matrix for model variants, with estimated cost and latency deltas per model pair and quantization profile.
- Runtime hooks: Lightweight client in serving runtime to call RPS and cache decisions for 1s for identical contexts.
- Console UI: New pages for budgets, SLAs and a cost dashboard.

API Changes (examples)
- New route config fields (YAML/JSON example):
  - route.sla.latency_p95_ms: 1200
  - route.sla.availability_pct: 99.5
  - route.budget.monthly_usd: 5000

DecisionEvent Schema (example table)
| field | description | type |
| route_id | internal route id | string |
| customer_id | customer id | string |
| model_attempted | primary model | string |
| model_selected | selected variant | string |
| cost_estimate_usd | estimated per-request cost | number |
| quality_delta_est | estimated relative quality change | number |

Performance and Scalability
- RPS must support 100k evaluations/sec at 99th percentile latency <= 15ms. We will implement multi-tenant sharding and local caching to meet the target.

Security and Privacy
- All routing calls only contain non-sensitive context (no prompt text). For customers that require Private deployment, RPS will run in customer VPC with a local policy store.

Compatibility and Migration
- Backwards-compatible defaults: routes without SLA/budget behave as before.
- Migration steps:
  1) Ship Schema: Accept new route fields but ignore until enabled.
  2) Console: Allow customers to opt-in per-route.
  3) Autosuggest policies: Default budget recommendations based on historical usage.

Roadmap and Themes (quarterly)
- Q1 2028: GA of Routing Policy Service, Reserved Plus pricing pilot, telemetry and console pages, canary with early enterprise customers.
- Q2 2028: Expand model compatibility catalog, add per-region budget controls, formal Dedicated SLA offering.
- Q3 2028: Integrations with Redwood Optimize for automated quantization recommendations tied to budget.
- Q4 2028: Marketplace SKUs and partner reseller billing.

Prioritization and Milestones
- M1 (2028-01-15): API schema landed and RPS prototype in staging.
- M2 (2028-02-28): Telemetry pipeline and decision event schema stable.
- M3 (2028-03-31): Console beta and Reserved Plus pilot with 3 customers.
- M4 (2028-05-15): GA and billing integration.

Pricing and Packaging Notes
New SKUs
- Reserved Plus (monthly commit): includes baseline reserved throughput, burst credits, and discounted off-peak unit pricing.
- Pay-as-you-go with Budget Cap: customers can set hard monthly caps which will trigger routing behavior to prioritize lower-cost model variants.

Pricing Guidance (examples)
- Reserved Plus: $X per reserved GPU-equivalent unit per month, includes 20% off-peak discount and 50% discount on burst units within commitment. Exact price will be set by Sales during pilot.
- PAYG with Budget Cap: base unit price unchanged, but customers who set hard caps will be subject to model selection optimizations to stay within budget.

Billing and Metering
- DecisionEvent-based metering: when fallback selects alternative model, billing records both attempted and selected model usage to allow crediting and downstream reconciliation.
- Invoices will include a breakdown by route, model family, and reserved vs burst usage.

Release Notes (v24 highlights)
- New: Routing Policy Service (RPS) with per-route SLA and budget fields.
- New: Reserved Plus pricing SKU (pilot).
- New: Cost-aware fallback engine available in Hosted and Dedicated modes.
- Improved: Console cost dashboards and per-route heatmaps.
- Changed: Runtime now calls RPS for routing decisions; 1s caching applied to reduce overhead.

Rollout Plan and Risk Mitigation
Phased Rollout
1) Internal dogfood and staging: 4 weeks of intensive validation including load, perf, and regression evals.
2) Closed Beta: 3 enterprise customers for Reserved Plus pilot with dedicated account managers.
3) Gradual Canary: 5% traffic on selected routes with automatic rollback on quality regression > 2% or latency P95 > SLA.
4) GA: Roll to all customers with feature flag opt-in for Private deployments.

Rollback Triggers
- Quality regression: >2% drop in eval score for a route over a 30-minute window.
- Latency breach: P95 > SLA for 2 consecutive 10-minute windows.
- Cost anomaly: Unexpected per-request cost > 3x estimate for >1% of requests.

Operational Runbook Summary
- Incident: RPS unavailable
  1) Fail open to last-known-good cached decision for 60s, then default to primary model.
  2) Pager on-call for eng-platform after alerts: routing-error-rate > 1% for 5 minutes.
  3) Postmortem: capture decision events and traces, analyze fallback frequency and root cause.

Appendices
A. Example route config
- name: realtime-chat
  model: redwood-fast-ft-1
  sla:
    latency_p95_ms: 300
    availability_pct: 99.9
  budget:
    monthly_usd: 2000

B. Decision event example (CSV)
- timestamp,route_id,customer_id,model_attempted,model_selected,cost_estimate_usd,quality_delta_est
- 2028-01-09T14:02:12Z,realtime-chat,cust-123,redwood-fast-ft-1,redwood-fast-q4,0.002, -0.01

C. Quick test checklist for canary
1) Generate 10k synthetic requests across 3 route profiles.
2) Confirm RPS P95 < 15ms and end-to-end P95 within SLA for 95% of windows.
3) Validate billing records accurately reflect selected model in invoice logs.
